newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to collar dogs with microchip tags.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to collar dogs with microchip tags.

text.p: Singapore said on Thursday all dogs on the island would soon be tagged with microchips.
The government's Primary Production Department (PPD) said the tags would help trace owners of the 5,000 stray dogs it impounds each year.
It could also help resolve disputed ownership, a spokeswoman for the PPD, which handles all agriculture, plant and animal matters, told Reuters.

Under the scheme, all of Singapore's 37,000 licensed dogs would have tiny microchips with unique identification numbers injected under the skin behind the left ear. The chips could then be read by hand-held scanners, she said.
A spokeswoman for Singapore's Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals said the group supported tagging because too many pet dogs were abandoned in Singapore.
The cost of tags would be borne by owners, she said.
